_comment: What every shipped real circuit is checked against, and the gate it has
to pass to be here at all.
A recovered layout is not a fact until something independent agrees with
it.  Two things do.  'length_m' is what the circuit publishes, and the
recovery solves its straights to land on it exactly, so that one is a
construction rather than a check.  'pole_s' is the real one: a pole lap
set on THIS layout by a car of the era this engine models.  A layout can
close, measure right and still be the wrong shape, and the lap time is
A circuit ships when its computed lap is within TOLERANCE_S of 'pole_s'.
Circuits with no comparable pole lap do not ship, however clean their
geometry -- unverified is not the same as correct.
tests/test_circuit_accuracy.py enforces this.  It is the honesty gate.
Recovered cleanly, held back, and why.  The survey set is a snapshot
from about 2019, so three of these are honest recordings of a layout
that no longer exists.  Correcting them would mean inventing the
rebuild.  Re-run tools/extract_circuits.py against current data and
